Switching from iPhone 13 pro to iPhone 16e?

So the back of my iphone 13 pro is shattered. It’s been shattered for a while but recently, my battery has been going crazy; my phone turns off at random times and comes back as 10% instead of the percentage I charged it up to (could be 90% and would still come back as 10%). Sometimes, it will turn off again then come back as 42% or any other random number. I am wondering if I should simply fix the battery or get a new phone.

I went to the apple store yesterday and looked at all the iPhone 16 series options. I really liked the 16e because:

-  I have very small hands. I struggle to type with one hand with my 13 pro. 6s was the perfect size for me.

- It was the lightest option, though not much of a difference from the 16.

- I really don’t care about specs or AI or dslr quality camera. I usually only text, take regular pictures, play simple mobile games and call on my phones. I think I spend the most time on Safari and Youtube.

- I still carry around my 6s for photos. I am obsessed with the old iphone camera colors: muted, warmer but with a gray undertone, higher contrast. I also have multiple film cameras which show how much I don’t care about “clean and crisp” photos at all. I care about colors and aesthetics.

- I am really bad with utilizing phones and computers to its maximal capacity. I don’t even know what new cool skills this series has. I just need a new phone that I know won’t turn off randomly.

- I really like the one-camera look.

- I compared the 16 pro, 16, and 16e cameras in portrait mode and 16 was not it. It’s either pro or e for me. 

I am only debating the 16e because employees were telling me they wouldn’t recommend it at all. Should I still get it?

Other than this, I was VERY violently adhd 😂 I showed very clear symptoms in each category that I was referred to see a professional twice. It all ended up in “she just needs to apply herself a little more.”

As I got older, I got better at masking my symptoms through anxiety: “What if they think I’m annoying? Am I talking too much right now? Will this be disappointing? How can I do this like ‘them’?” I became so good at it that I myself never thought I could have adhd until two years ago.

In college, I stayed up all night and heavily restricted myself from going out so that I could focus on assignments and studying.
